newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - U.S. T-bond volatilities tumble.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - U.S. T-bond volatilities tumble.

text.p: Implied volatilities for U.S. Treasury bond options tumbled as bond prices recouped early losses and the market took out the event-risk premium for the U.S. elections, dealers said.
Implied volatility for December T-bond futures options fell nearly a full point to 9.0 percent from about 9.9 at Tuesday's close.
"Especially with the auction coming, I'm really surprised that they hit it like they did," said a brokerage firm trader at the Chicago Board of Trade (CBOT).

The Treasury is due to auction $10 billion of 30-year bonds on Thursday in the third and final leg of its quarterly refunding. The 10-year note auction today produced an average yield of 6.273 percent, largely in line with expectations.

Still, the weight of the fresh supply was felt late in the day, and December T-bond futures were off 6/32 at 113-19/32 in late trade after bouncing from early lows to hover near 114-00 for most of the day.
December 113 puts and 115 calls were actively traded.
"I guess people are looking for a move one way or the other," the CBOT trader said.

December options expire on November 15. With January options going on board next Monday and March contracts still too long-dated for gamma players, traders said there was good demand for FLEX options, which are contracts whose terms can be negotiated individually.
The re-election of President Bill Clinton and the Republicans' retention of a congressional majority were in line with broadly shared expectations, traders said.
"Status quo, I think," said a Eurodollar trader for a brokerage firm at the Chicago Mercantile Exchange (CME). "People are pretty content with the way things were."

Implied volatilities for CME Eurodollar futures options were mostly steady. Volatility for March options was just below late Tuesday levels at around 12.0 percent, while June and further out were slightly better bid.

December and March Eurodollar futures were pinned very close to 95.50, reflecting growing expectations that the three-month Eurodollar deposit rate would stay steady at 5.5 percent for a while, traders said.
The market was shifting its focus to next week's inflation data, with the producer prices index due out on Wednesday and the consumer price index on Thursday.

The CME trader said little action was expected until Tuesday, with CME interest rate products closing early on Monday in observance of the Veterans Day. CME contracts will trade normal hours on Friday.
CBOT T-bond contracts will close early on Friday, but trade normal hours on Monday.
